lesson_title: The Flash That Ended a War
hook_text: At 8:15 one August morning, a single bomb destroyed a city. Three weeks later, World War II was over.
clip_script: 1945. American forces are closing in on Japan, island by island. The fighting is savage. On Okinawa, tens of thousands die. Fire bombs burn Tokyo. Still, Japan's generals will not surrender. Meanwhile, in the New Mexico desert, scientists test a weapon no one has seen before. The flash is brighter than the sun. On 6 August, a bomber named the Enola Gay drops one bomb on Hiroshima. By the end of the year, about 140 000 people are dead. Two days later the Soviet Union declares war and attacks in Manchuria. On 9 August, a second bomb falls on Nagasaki. On 15 August, the emperor speaks on the radio for the first time: Japan will surrender. On 2 September, it signs. The war is over. But a new age has begun, one in which a single weapon can erase a city.
visual_style: A map of the Pacific with island stepping stones; a desert at dawn with a sudden white flash; a clock stopped at 8:15; the ruined dome in Hiroshima; a battleship deck with a signing table.
pacing: Steady build to the flash, a long silence, then a measured close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn when, where, why and how World War II ended.
